findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/Spectrum/Prime/Basic.lean:509-513 defines the `MulAction G (PrimeSpectrum R)` with `asIdeal_smul : (g • P).asIdeal = g • P.asIdeal`; the file's own docstring at line 70 concedes "these morphisms form a right action".
findings.fix: Define `translate g := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (MulSemiringAction.toRingEquiv G A g⁻¹).toRingHom)`, so `translate_base_apply` reads `= g • x` and `translate_mul` becomes the left action `translate (g * h) = translate h ≫ translate g`; or keep the definition and rename to something contravariant (e.g. `specComap`), dropping the "translate" wording.
findings.issue: `translate A G g` advertises translation by `g`, but `translate_apply` (line 84) proves `(translate A G g).base x = g⁻¹ • x`: it is translation by `g⁻¹` with respect to Mathlib's canonical left action `MulAction G (PrimeSpectrum R)`, hence `translate_mul` (line 71) is an anti-homomorphism. A consumer reading `translate A G g` will take the wrong point map.

findings.evidence: Mathlib names such lemmas with `_base_apply`: mathlib/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/ProjectiveSpectrum/Scheme.lean:664 `toSpec_base_apply_eq_comap`; map-level form mathlib/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Scheme.lean:538 `Spec.map_base`.
findings.fix: Rename to `translate_base_apply` (or `translate_base` for the map-level form).
findings.issue: `translate_apply` states a fact about `(translate A G g).base` applied to a point, not about `translate` applied to an argument; `_apply` per the suffix convention means `foo x = …`.

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Scheme.lean:490 defines `Spec.algebraMap`; lemmas about it are named after it, e.g. mathlib/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/AffineScheme.lean:1295 `Spec.algebraMap_stalkIso_inv`. Only hit for `structureMap` in Mathlib is mathlib/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/RestrictedProduct/Basic.lean:130.
findings.fix: Rename to `projection_specAlgebraMap` (namespace folded in per the convention, since bare `algebraMap` is ambiguous).
findings.issue: `projection_structureMap` names its right factor "structureMap", which is not the declaration in the statement (`Spec.algebraMap R (FixedPoints.subalgebra R A G)`); `structureMap` in Mathlib is `RestrictedProduct.structureMap`, unrelated. Inconsistent with `translate_projection` (line 94), which names its factor after the declaration.

findings.evidence: Mathlib's corresponding instances are anonymous: mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/Invariant/Basic.lean:78-79 `instance (H : Subgroup G) … : Algebra.IsInvariant A (FixedPoints.subalgebra A B H) (G ⧸ H)`; mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Subalgebra/Operations.lean:110 `instance : SMulCommClass G (FixedPoints.subalgebra A B' G) B'`.
findings.fix: Move it into the `TauCeti.Algebra.IsInvariant` namespace beside `finite_of_finiteType` and leave it anonymous, as Mathlib's analogues are.
findings.issue: `TauCeti.MulSemiringAction.fixedPointsSubalgebraIsInvariant` is an `Algebra.IsInvariant` instance about `FixedPoints.subalgebra`, filed in the `MulSemiringAction` namespace (whose other contents are `charpoly` lemmas) and carrying a stuttering class suffix; nobody searching for it will look there.

summary: `translate g` is named for translation by `g` but its base map is `g⁻¹ • ·`, the inverse of Mathlib's existing left action on `PrimeSpectrum`; plus two convention slips (`translate_apply` for a `.base` lemma, `structureMap` for `Spec.algebraMap`) and an invariance instance filed under the `MulSemiringAction` namespace.
